source_title: Personas Make Users Memorable for Product Team Members (Nielsen Norman Group)
publication_date_if_available: 2015-02-16 (date taken from a citing page, not shown in the excerpt I read)
key_finding_or_summary: Says personas should be based on user research, are most useful early in design, and add details such as experience level with the product once distinct roles emerge. Also says personas can be used to segment analytics data.
relevance_to_milestone: Obj 1-2: justifies experience level and role as core persona fields; supports the point that real personas need research grounding.
limitations: Read via a search-result excerpt, not the full article. Practitioner guidance, not a controlled study. It describes research-based personas, which synthetic personas are not.

source_title: Book review: Personas - User Focused Design by Lene Nielsen (QCRI Persona blog)
research_topic: User personas and persona modeling; limitations
key_finding_or_summary: The review says personas are fictitious but derived from knowledge of multiple real users, and notes that persona users bring their own cultural prejudices to interpreting them.
relevance_to_milestone: Obj 1: supports the distinction between research-derived and invented personas; supports caution about stereotyping.
limitations: Secondary review of a book I did not read directly. No publication date found in the excerpt.

research_topic: Persona limitations; sources of persona information
key_finding_or_summary: Lists information sources for personas (contextual interviews, informal discussions, product documents, formal interviews and surveys) and drawbacks: one instance stands for a whole segment, validity of the profile is uncertain, and story-based methods lack credibility in some circles.
relevance_to_milestone: Obj 1: concise list of persona limitations and data sources; informs the limitations column and README.
limitations: Course notes, not peer-reviewed. Undated in the excerpt.

source_title: Are personas done? Evaluating their usefulness in the age of digital analytics (Salminen et al., Persona Studies)
key_finding_or_summary: A conceptual critique arguing that personas sit between aggregated and individual statistics, and discussing persona validation, inconsistency and long development times.
relevance_to_milestone: Obj 1-2: grounds the limitation that personas need validation and can be inconsistent.
limitations: Conceptual argument, not an empirical test. Focused on digital marketing and analytics. I read only the abstract page.

source_title: Instilling Knowledge Claims of Personas from 346 Research Articles (Salminen et al., CHI EA 2021)
research_topic: Persona limitations; state of persona research
key_finding_or_summary: Extracted 130 knowledge claims from 346 persona articles. Claims about persona definition show more consensus, while persona creation and use contain a high proportion of unverified claims.
relevance_to_milestone: Obj 1-2: supports treating persona creation practices, including mine, as lightly evidenced design choices.
limitations: Extended abstract; I read the abstract only. It does not evaluate LLM-generated personas.

source_title: When to Use Which User-Experience Research Methods (Nielsen Norman Group)
research_topic: UX research methods; behavioral vs attitudinal
key_finding_or_summary: Says UX methods range from lab usability testing to unmoderated assessments, that most projects benefit from combining several methods, and that methods can be mapped along behavioral/attitudinal and qualitative/quantitative axes.
relevance_to_milestone: Obj 1: frames where synthetic personas fit among UX methods (they cannot supply behavioral evidence).
limitations: I read search excerpts, not the full article. Publication date not shown in the excerpt.

key_finding_or_summary: Describes usability testing as observing real users attempting tasks. Core elements are facilitator, tasks and participant. Recommends about five participants for a typical qualitative study of a single user group, and distinguishes moderated from unmoderated tests.
relevance_to_milestone: Obj 1; later milestones: informs how personas will later be used to mimic test participants. Not used in this milestone's data beyond context.
limitations: Government guidance that cites NN/g rather than primary research. Not Figma-specific.

source_title: Synthetic Users: AI 'Participants' (Nielsen Norman Group video page)
research_topic: Synthetic users; limits of AI-generated research
key_finding_or_summary: NN/g's summary line says synthetic users are fake users generated by AI and that, while a few use cases may exist, user research needs real users.
relevance_to_milestone: Obj 1-2: supports labelling every persona as synthetic and not claiming it represents real Figma users.
limitations: This is a short video summary page. I did not read the full NN/g article it links to, so I cite no detail from the article itself.

source_title: Evaluating Large Language Models in Generating Synthetic HCI Research Data: a Case Study (Hamalainen, Tavast, Kunnari; CHI 2023)
key_finding_or_summary: GPT-3 produced believable open-ended questionnaire responses about video games as art. The authors conclude synthetic data may help ideate and pilot experiments, but findings must be validated with real data.
relevance_to_milestone: Obj 1-2: supports using synthetic personas for piloting only, with real-data validation noted as a requirement.
limitations: One topic (video games as art), GPT-3, and self-report text. Not usability testing and not design tools.

source_title: Out of One, Many: Using Language Models to Simulate Human Samples (Argyle et al.)
publication_date_if_available: 2022-09 (inferred from arXiv ID 2209.06899; later published in Political Analysis per BYU page)
key_finding_or_summary: Showed that conditioning GPT-3 on socio-demographic backstories from real survey participants could emulate response distributions of human subgroups ('algorithmic fidelity') in US survey settings.
relevance_to_milestone: Obj 1-2: shows that persona conditioning can matter, but only with real backstories in a survey domain.
limitations: US political and survey domain with GPT-3 and real participant backstories. It does not show that role/skill-prompted personas mirror Figma users.

source_title: Generative Agent Simulations of 1,000 People (Park et al., arXiv 2411.10109)
key_finding_or_summary: Built agents for 1,052 real people from qualitative interviews. They matched participants' General Social Survey answers about 85% as well as participants matched their own answers two weeks later, and showed less accuracy bias across racial and ideological groups than agents given only demographic descriptions.
relevance_to_milestone: Obj 1-2: supports the design choice to favor grounded, role- and behavior-based attributes over thin demographic descriptions, and illustrates how personas can be evaluated against real people.
limitations: Agents were grounded in two-hour interviews with real people, which this project does not have. The result does not transfer to rule-based or prompt-only personas.

source_title: Marked Personas: Using Natural Language Prompts to Measure Stereotypes in Language Models (Cheng, Durmus, Jurafsky; ACL 2023)
key_finding_or_summary: Found that personas generated by GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 contained higher rates of racial stereotypes than human-written portrayals from the same prompts, with patterns of othering for marginalized groups.
relevance_to_milestone: Obj 1-2: the main reason the schema omits age, gender, ethnicity and similar demographic fields.
limitations: Studied specific models and demographic prompts; does not address professional-role personas directly.

source_title: Guide to Dev Mode (Figma Help Center)
key_finding_or_summary: Documents Dev Mode: an inspect panel with specs, compare-changes, links to resources, ready-for-dev handoff statuses, and a Figma for VS Code extension.
relevance_to_milestone: Obj 2: supports the feature scope listed for developer personas (P005, P006, P014).
limitations: Documentation describes features, not how real users behave. Figma may have changed this page since access date.

source_title: Dev Mode for admins (Figma Help Center)
research_topic: Figma product context: seat types and permissions
key_finding_or_summary: States that anyone with a Full or Dev seat can access Dev Mode, and that developers on a free View seat can still do basic inspection such as viewing properties and measurements, copying code and exporting assets.
relevance_to_milestone: Obj 2: supports permission-related usability constraints, for example P005's view-only access.
limitations: Seat details and plan rules can change. Check the current page before relying on them.

research_topic: Figma product context: core design features
key_finding_or_summary: The section covers using auto layout, with the Figma Learn navigation listing the Figma product family (Design, Make, Dev Mode, Slides, Sites, Buzz, Draw) and related articles on components.
relevance_to_milestone: Obj 2: supports naming auto layout and components as in-scope features and the existence of the other Figma products referenced by personas.
limitations: I read search excerpts of the section and navigation, not each article in full.

source_title: Design tools and shapes (Figma Help Center section)
research_topic: Figma product context: core design features
key_finding_or_summary: The section lists layers, frames, text, fonts and fills guides for Figma Design, and the page navigation mentions an accessibility help area.
relevance_to_milestone: Obj 2: supports the layers, frames, text and fills features assigned to beginner personas.
limitations: Excerpt-level reading only. The mention of accessibility help is a navigation label; I did not assess Figma's actual accessibility support.
